title: Playing without the piano, retiring in 1959 and carnival ball patrons
summary: DeDroit says he quit leading in 1959 and complains of carnival-ball patrons' demands and costs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: You know? He just played the wrong instrument. I did the same thing at the Gulfport Institute over there, college over there, military school. The piano was so bad that the saxophones' mouthpiece were falling. I said, shove him in. Don't play the piano. No one knew that he didn't play the piano all night. So then the portable pianist came out. And Russ Papaya bought himself one. And I was about to buy one. But I decided to quit the pianist to get my voice away. And it canceled. She was so sick. So I quit. And so I quit in 59. I quit. And so I quit in 59. I had calls and calls and calls and wanted me to play, but I said, I don't have any music. I get current in music. I make current to lead the band. I didn't miss it. It's a funny thing to say, how could you retire after all that? You get enough of that too. You get enough of that excitement. I'm going to go. I'm going to tell you the union ought to make the price of carnival balls so high that they wouldn't have any carnival balls. Those people have daydreams up to you. And they want you to put up the music, and you want to give you twelve musicians, and they want you to play Pagliacci all night, you know, and all the big operas. And then when they do the dance, call out, then you've got to be a jack. They don't know. I mean I hire a violin player and I pay them about thirty or forty dollars to play one tune. But remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember to remember Then sometime I'd have to hire him in from the symphony. I had a man play for me, and I play his first trumpet with the Philadelphia Symphony.
